primitives.name: Correlation Impact on Optimal Fractions
primitives.verbatim_quote: Key qualitative result: positive correlation between investments reduces optimal fractions; negative correlation increases them.
primitives.assumptions: Investment returns are jointly normally distributed or sufficiently symmetric.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-Gaussian or heavy-tailed return distributions invalidate this rule.

reasoning_traces.think:
The generalized Kelly criterion extends the classical single-gamble formulation to portfolios by deriving an exact first-order condition on expected log wealth. For L investments, it requires solving ∫ k_l(x_l)·p(x)/(1 + Σ_{l'} f_{l'}·k_{l'}(x_{l'})) dx = 0. This nonlinear integral equation defines the optimal allocation vector f. Linearizing around small parameters yields M·f = b, where M encodes second moments and b contains first moments. Correlations shift these allocations: positive correlation lowers optimal fractions, while negative correlation raises them. However, this moment-based linearization fails for large edges or asymmetric payoffs typical in sports betting. Thus, GSE applies the full nonlinear condition post-constraint enforcement to avoid leverage-induced blowups.
